front: What is Express Error Handler in one sentence?
back: One-line: four-argument middleware (err, req, res, next) must be registered last — centralize status codes, hide stacks in prod, never leak internals.

front: Explain the mental model of Express Error Handler (how the system thinks).
back: Express distinguishes error-handling middleware by arity (4 params). Calling next(err) or throwing inside async route (with wrapper) skips normal middleware and jumps to error handler.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Express Error Handler?
back: Request → parsers → routes → 404 factory → GLOBAL ERROR HANDLER (4 args) → next(err) lands here → Express 5: native async error propagation — verify your version.

front: Symptom: Stack trace in prod JSON — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NODE_ENV · Fix: Gate stack on development only

front: Symptom: 404 returns HTML not JSON — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Error handler after static middleware order · Fix: Move API routes + 404 before static; separate routers

front: Symptom: Async route hangs, no log — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing catch(next) · Fix: Wrap async handlers

front: Symptom: headers already sent — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Double res.send in error path · Fix: if (res.headersSent) return next(err)

front: Symptom: Validation errors inconsistent — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Ad-hoc status codes · Fix: Centralize in error class + handler

front: Symptom: Error handler never runs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Only 3-arg middleware registered · Fix: Must be (err, req, res, next)

front: Gotcha with Express Error Handler: what silently fails?
back: Order matters — error handler after all app.use routes; 404 handler before error handler.

front: When should you NOT use Express Error Handler?
back: Per-route try/catch everywhere — duplicates logic; use wrapper + global handler. Sending err.stack to clients in any environment — security finding every time.

front: What is Express route regular expressions in one sentence?
back: Express path patterns are not full JavaScript RegExp — anchoring, capture groups, and * semantics differ; misread routes cause 404s, open redirects, and ReDoS.

front: Explain the mental model of Express route regular expressions (how the system thinks).
back: Express compiles route strings into an internal matcher (via path-to-regexp). A route like /users/:id is anchored to the full path segment unless you opt into regex or wildcards.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Express route regular expressions?
back: Request: GET /api/users/42/settings → Route '/users/:id' → matches /users/42 only (one segment for :id) → Route '/users/:id(*)' → :id captures rest including slashes (legacy) → Route /^\/users\/(\d+)$/ → full RegExp route — YOU own anchors ^ $

front: Given a broken Express route regular expressions setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Request: GET /api/users/42/settings

front: Symptom: Route never matches — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing anchors on RegExp route; typo in param regex · Fix: Add ^...$; test with req.path logging

front: Symptom: Wrong handler runs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Route order — /:id before /new · Fix: Register static paths first

front: Symptom: :id eats too much — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Greedy .+ in custom regex · Fix: Restrict charset: [^/]+ or (\\d+)

front: Symptom: 404 on valid URL — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Router mount path doubled · Fix: Mount at /api + route /users → /api/users

front: Symptom: %2F in param breaks — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Decoded slash splits segments · Fix: Avoid slashes in params; use query string

front: Symptom: Express 5 vs 4 splat change — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: * / (*) syntax migration · Fix: Check Express version docs for wildcard routes

front: Symptom: Performance spike on some URLs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Catastrophic backtracking in regex · Fix: Simplify pattern; cap length; use string routes

front: Symptom: req.params empty on RegExp route — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Used anonymous groups incorrectly · Fix: Use named string routes or parse req.path

front: Gotcha with Express route regular expressions: what silently fails?
back: Inline (regex) must be parenthesized and escaped for backslashes — in JS strings: '/:id(\\d+)' (double backslash).

front: When should you NOT use Express route regular expressions?
back: Complex URL parsing — use a dedicated router (e.g. explicit path parser) instead of nested regex. Validation as routing — route should identify resource; validate body/query in middleware (express query handler). Open-ended user-defined regex — never compile user input into RegExp routes (ReDoS + bypass).
